paper_title: Feedback Friction LLMs Struggle to Fully Incorporate External Feedback
caption: : GPQA confidence vs. accuracy
model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and accuracy for three different accuracy metrics – ‘Final Accuracy’, ‘Δ Accuracy’, and ‘Initial Accuracy’ – represented as lines with error bars. The x-axis, labeled “Initial Confidence,” utilizes a linear scale ranging from 0.91 to 0.99 with tick intervals of 0.01, indicating confidence levels on a scale from 91% to 99%. The y-axis, labeled “Accuracy Confidence”, is also linear and ranges from 0.91 to 1.00 with tick intervals of 0.01, representing accuracy levels.  The ‘Final Accuracy’ line, depicted in blue, begins at approximately 0.94 and steadily decreases to 0.96, with a minimum value of 0.958 at x = 0.93. The ‘Δ Accuracy’ line, colored orange and displayed as a dashed line, starts at approximately 0.92 and generally declines, reaching a minimum value of 0.912 at x = 0.92. The ‘Initial Accuracy’ line, shown in green and represented by a dotted line, commences at approximately 0.96 and gradually decreases to 0.97, with a minimum value of 0.966 at x = 0.98.  Each line is accompanied by error bars, representing the standard deviation of the accuracy measurements at each initial confidence level.
